chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan as-Saffar related to him via his chain, from al-Abbas ibn Yazid, who said: One day, I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): May I be your ransom, what is the meaning of Allah's exalted saying: 'And when you see it, you see bliss and a great kingdom'?

He said to me: When Allah admits the people of Paradise into Paradise, He sends a messenger to one of His disciples, and he finds the doorkeepers at his door, who say to him: Wait until we seek permission for you. And the messenger of Allah does not reach him except with permission, and this is His saying: 'And when you see it, you see bliss and a great kingdom'.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'you see bliss and a great kingdom' in Surah Al-Insan?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Fadail al-Shia* interprets Quran 76:20 as describing the exalted status of the *Awliya* in Paradise, where their authority is so profound that even Allah’s messenger must seek permission from their doorkeepers to enter. This highlights the Shia concept of *Wilayah* extending into the afterlife, emphasizing the hierarchical dignity and intercessory power of the saints. The scene illustrates that the 'great kingdom' refers not just to material bliss, but to the spiritual sovereignty granted to the faithful servants of God.
